# Accessibility

Free and freemium tools that use AI or on-device recognition to support low vision, blindness, deafness, hard of hearing, speech differences, and everyday access. These tools can be genuinely useful, but none is perfect or a replacement for professional accessibility services.

**Last verified:** October 22, 2026 · **12 tools**

[Back to the guide](../README.md) · [All categories](README.md) · [Safety checklist](../free-tier-safety.md)

> **Category tip:** Try accessibility tools before you need them, in the light and noise conditions where you actually use them. Keep a backup method for critical tasks such as medication labels, emergency alerts, or workplace communication. Do not let a free app become the only path to essential information.

**Start here:** [Seeing AI](#tool-seeing-ai) · [Be My Eyes](#tool-be-my-eyes) · [Live Transcribe & Sound Notifications](#tool-live-transcribe)

## All 12 tools

<a id="tool-seeing-ai"></a>

### Seeing AI

`Free` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** A free Microsoft app for iOS that narrates short text, documents, people, scenes, products, and currency to support everyday tasks.
- **Sign-up notes:** Free App Store download; no account or card. Requires a supported iPhone or iPad.
- **Limits:** Features and language support vary by device and region. Recognition can fail in poor light or complex scenes, and it should not be trusted alone for medication, navigation, or safety decisions.
- **Best for:** Reading mail, labels, and packaging or getting a quick description of a scene.
- **Official link:** <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/ai/seeing-ai>
- **Tags:** `blind` `low-vision` `scene-description` `ios`

<a id="tool-be-my-eyes"></a>

### Be My Eyes

`Free` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** A free app connecting blind and low-vision users with sighted volunteers and AI descriptions of photos or live scenes.
- **Sign-up notes:** Free account and app; no card. AI description fair-use limits apply.
- **Limits:** AI descriptions have fair-use limits and can be wrong; volunteer availability varies. Humans may see what you share, so avoid exposing sensitive documents or banking details.
- **Best for:** Getting quick human or AI help reading a label, matching clothing, or checking a setting.
- **Official link:** <https://www.bemyeyes.com>
- **Tags:** `blind` `low-vision` `volunteers` `ai-description`

---

<a id="tool-google-lookout"></a>

### Google Lookout

`Free` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** A free Android app that uses the camera and AI to identify currency, read text, explore scenes, and find objects in supported regions.
- **Sign-up notes:** Free Play Store download; no card. Supported Android devices and regions only.
- **Limits:** Supported modes, devices, and languages vary. Recognition is not perfect and should not be used as the only method for navigation or safety-critical decisions.
- **Best for:** Everyday Android assistance with reading, products, and scene descriptions.
- **Official link:** <https://www.google.com/accessibility/products-features/>
- **Tags:** `blind` `low-vision` `android` `scene-description`

<a id="tool-live-transcribe"></a>

### Live Transcribe & Sound Notifications

`Free` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** A free Android app and built-in accessibility tool for real-time speech captions and sound alerts such as doorbells, alarms, or a name being called.
- **Sign-up notes:** Free Play Store download or built-in Android tool; no account or card.
- **Limits:** Accuracy depends on language, microphone, noise, and dialect. Some features need downloads or connectivity. Do not rely on it alone for emergencies or critical instructions.
- **Best for:** Following in-person conversations and being alerted to important sounds.
- **Official link:** <https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.audio.hearing.visualization.accessibility.scribe>
- **Tags:** `deaf` `hard-of-hearing` `captions` `android`

<a id="tool-envision"></a>

### Envision AI

`Free tier` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** A free app for scanning documents, reading text, recognizing scenes, and getting AI descriptions, with a usable free allowance.
- **Sign-up notes:** Free app and free account; no card. Premium features require a subscription.
- **Limits:** Free usage and advanced AI features are limited; higher volume and premium features require a subscription. Accuracy varies with image quality and content.
- **Best for:** Reading documents and exploring everyday images with a mix of on-device and AI tools.
- **Official link:** <https://www.letsenvision.com>
- **Tags:** `low-vision` `document-reading` `ocr` `mobile`

<a id="tool-supersense"></a>

### SuperSense

`Free tier` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** A free AI app for blind users with modes for reading, finding objects, recognizing currency, and exploring scenes.
- **Sign-up notes:** Free app with an optional account; no card for the free tier. Paid plans add features.
- **Limits:** Free features and usage are limited; some capabilities require a paid plan. Recognition can miss obstacles or make unsafe guesses. Use a mobility aid and training.
- **Best for:** Quick object and text recognition on an iPhone or Android device.
- **Official link:** <https://supersense.app>
- **Tags:** `blind` `object-recognition` `reading` `mobile`

<a id="tool-microsoft-translator"></a>

### Microsoft Translator

`Free` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** Free text, camera, speech, and conversation translation across many languages, including a conversation mode for two speakers.
- **Sign-up notes:** Free app or web use; no card for personal use. A Microsoft account may be optional for some features.
- **Limits:** Personal free usage is subject to fair-use limits; some features, offline language packs, or larger business use may require adjustments. Translation can miss nuance and context.
- **Best for:** Cross-language conversations, travel, and understanding short written or photographed text.
- **Official link:** <https://translator.microsoft.com>
- **Tags:** `translation` `speech` `camera` `conversation`

<a id="tool-google-voice-access"></a>

### Voice Access

`Free` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** A free Android accessibility service that lets you control your phone by speaking commands, with numbered labels for on-screen controls.
- **Sign-up notes:** Free Play Store download; no account or card. Android only.
- **Limits:** Language and Android support vary, and setup takes practice. Background noise can cause errors, and some commands or apps may not work as expected.
- **Best for:** Hands-free Android phone control when touch is difficult or uncomfortable.
- **Official link:** <https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.android.apps.accessibility.voiceaccess>
- **Tags:** `voice-control` `motor` `android` `hands-free`

<a id="tool-apple-voice-control"></a>

### Apple Voice Control

`Free` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** A free built-in accessibility feature for supported Apple devices that lets you navigate and type using spoken commands.
- **Sign-up notes:** Built into supported Apple devices; no account or card.
- **Limits:** Requires a supported device and setup; command availability varies by OS and app. Speech recognition can struggle with noise, accents, or unusual words.
- **Best for:** Hands-free control of an iPhone, iPad, or Mac without buying extra software.
- **Official link:** <https://www.apple.com/accessibility/features/>
- **Tags:** `voice-control` `motor` `apple` `built-in`

<a id="tool-windows-live-captions"></a>

### Windows Live Captions

`Free` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** A free built-in Windows 11 feature that automatically captions audio playing on the PC, with broader language support on newer systems.
- **Sign-up notes:** Built into Windows 11; no account or card. Some languages need a download.
- **Limits:** Requires a compatible Windows version, may need language downloads, and does not caption every sound or app. Accuracy varies with audio quality and language.
- **Best for:** Adding on-screen captions to meetings, videos, or audio on Windows without extra software.
- **Official link:** <https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accessibility/windows/use-live-captions-to-better-understand-audio>
- **Tags:** `deaf` `hard-of-hearing` `captions` `windows`

<a id="tool-apple-live-captions"></a>

### Apple Live Captions

`Free` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** A free built-in iPhone, iPad, and Mac feature that generates captions for audio from apps, calls, and conversations on supported devices.
- **Sign-up notes:** Built into supported Apple devices; no account or card. Beta or region limits may apply.
- **Limits:** Available on supported devices and languages; some features require newer hardware or are still labeled beta. Captions can lag or mishear, especially with names and jargon.
- **Best for:** On-device captions during calls, videos, and face-to-face conversations on Apple devices.
- **Official link:** <https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/get-live-captions-of-spoken-audio-iphe0990f7bb/ios>
- **Tags:** `deaf` `hard-of-hearing` `captions` `apple`

<a id="tool-chrome-live-caption"></a>

### Chrome Live Caption

`Free` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** A free, on-device Chrome feature that automatically captions audio and video played in the browser, with optional translation in some versions.
- **Sign-up notes:** Built into Chrome; no account or card. Some languages and devices are unsupported.
- **Limits:** Language support and availability depend on Chrome version and device. Some content, DRM-protected media, or system audio may not be captioned accurately.
- **Best for:** Adding captions to web videos and browser audio without another tool.
- **Official link:** <https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/10538231>
- **Tags:** `deaf` `hard-of-hearing` `captions` `chrome`
